intended_object: The group isomorphism Spin(Q₁) ≅ Spin(Q₂) induced by an isometry equivalence (M₁,Q₁) ≅ (M₂,Q₂) of quadratic modules. It is the restriction of the induced isomorphism of Clifford algebras. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The forward map is `e.toIsometry.spinGroupMap`, which restricts `CliffordAlgebra.map e` to `spinGroup Q₁`. The inverse map is the same construction for `e.symm`. The two proof obligations follow from functoriality: `spinGroupMap_comp` and `spinGroupMap_id`. So the definition is the usual isomorphism of Spin groups induced by functoriality of the Clifford algebra.

The setting is a commutative ring R with modules over it. That is the same generality in which Mathlib defines `spinGroup`, so it is the natural one.

Mathlib's `SpinGroup.lean` has no induced map or equivalence between Spin groups, so there is no counterpart to cite.
